findings.title: New assignment_source kwarg breaks existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now unconditionally calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), including when the value is None. Existing IssueSyncIntegration implementations such as the Jira, GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps integrations define sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True) without **kwargs or an assignment_source parameter, so every outbound assignee task for those providers will raise TypeError instead of syncing and will be retried until exhaustion. The added tests mask this because ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound is replaced with a MagicMock that accepts any arguments. Either update all implementations to accept the new parameter or avoid passing it to implementations that do not support it.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass field is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now(), which executes timezone.now() once when the class is defined rather than when each AssignmentSource is created. Every source created by a long-lived process therefore carries the same increasingly stale import-time timestamp instead of its actual queueing time, making the field incorrect for logging, debugging, or any future staleness/expiry check. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) instead.

findings.title: AssignmentSource queued datetime is not round-trip safe through the outbound task payload
findings.body: assignment_source.to_dict() returns the queued value as a datetime object, and that dict is placed directly into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs. After task transport/JSON serialization the value arrives as a string, but AssignmentSource.from_dict does not parse it back, so the reconstructed object violates its declared queued: datetime type and round-tripping to_dict()/from_dict() is not type-preserving. Serialize queued as an ISO-formatted string and parse it in from_dict, or remove queued from the serialized payload.

findings.title: No test proves non-matching integrations still sync or that inbound deassign is suppressed
findings.body: The only new matching-source test covers assign through GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly. There is no test with an AssignmentSource whose integration_id differs from the target integration, so a regression in which should_sync returns False for any non-None source would still pass even though the PR intends other integrations to keep receiving outbound updates. There is also no mocked/eager-task assertion for the inbound deassign path in sync_group_assignee_inbound, so forgetting to propagate assignment_source there would not be caught. Add non-matching-source assign/deassign cases asserting sync_assignee_outbound is still called, and a matching-source deassign/inbound-deassign case asserting it is not.
